bulletin.night: The Northern Limit of Monsoon continues to pass through 18°N/60°E, 18°N/65°E, 18°N/70°E, Harnai, Solapur, Hyderabad, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Kalingapatnam, Paradeep, Baripada, Purulia, Dhanbad, Muzaffarpur and 28.3°N/83°E as on 13 th June, 2026. Conditions are favourable for further advance of southwest monsoon into more parts of Maharashtra, remaining parts of Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, some more parts of Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar and some parts of South Chhattisgarh during next 4-5 days.

met_analysis:
The Northern Limit of Monsoon continues to pass through 18°N/60°E, 18°N/65°E, 18°N/70°E, Harnai, Solapur, Hyderabad, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Kalingapatnam, Paradeep, Baripada, Purulia, Dhanbad, Muzaffarpur and 28.3°N/83°E.
Conditions are favourable for further advance of southwest monsoon into more parts of Maharashtra, remaining parts of Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, some more parts of Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar and some parts of South Chhattisgarh during next 4-5 days.
The seasonal trough at mean sea level from West Rajasthan to Gangetic West Bengal across northeast Rajasthan, north Madhya Pradesh, south Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand persists.
The trough in lower tropospheric westerlies now runs roughly along Long. 88°E to the north of Lat. 22°N at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over south coastal Odisha adjoining north Coastal Andhra Pradesh at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The trough from West central Bay of Bengal off south coastal Andhra Pradesh to south Tamil Nadu now runs from the above cyclonic circulation over south coastal Odisha adjoining north Coastal Andhra Pradesh to south Tamil Nadu across southwest Bay of Bengal at 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The trough from central Uttar Pradesh to north Madhya Maharashtra across West Madhya Pradesh at 5.8 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough in upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 12.6 km above mean sea level roughly along Long.
73°E to the north of Lat. 30°N persists.
